content.comment_body: I'm out of marker flags in my code. I noticed there are 'X' coils available—can those be used as flags? The manual only mentions that unused block connectors are marked with an X.

No, 'open terminal' (X-connectors) are not flags. They act as closures for digital outputs in the output block. Without completing the digital outputs for blocks, the program cannot be loaded into the [product_name].

Hello, you might want to review your code to avoid running out of marker bits. Sometimes, unused outputs can serve as extra marker bits. You can upload your code (as a zip), and we can look for ways to free more markers, if you're allowed to share your program.
Thanks [user_name]. If I ever need more flags, I could use unused coils. By the way, can X-connectors be used with text message boxes? I haven't tried it. Usually, I use an M flag as output for them.
For every box that has a digital output.
Hello [user_name], yes, text boxes need to be completed with either an M, X, or output. You can also use an OR box to group up to four text boxes and connect them to one M or X.
I've connected several text boxes to a single M before. I'm working in ladder diagram, so I don't use the logic functions available in FBD. Thanks for the tips!

analysis.insight_summary: Community members explored ways to manage limited marker flags in a [product_name] module. Initial inquiries revealed confusion about X-connectors, prompting clarifications that X-connectors are output closures, not extra flags. Users suggested strategies to save on marker usage, including repurposing unused outputs and combining message boxes, aiming for more efficiency when programming.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to expand the number of marker flags available in their [product_name] program. Their goal is to clarify the roles of system connectors (X-connectors specifically) and find practical, flexible solutions for linking message boxes inside the software.
